newsitem.title: AUSTRIA: Austria voices grave concern over Albania.
newsitem.headline: Austria voices grave concern over Albania.

text.p: Austria on Tuesday voiced grave concern over the situation in Albania, where emergency rule was introduced in an effort to quell a wave of violent unrest that has swept the Balkan nation.
In a statement by Foreign Minister Wolfgang Schuessel, it urged President Sali Berisha and all political forces in the country to work together to resolve the crisis in a peaceful way.

"The foreign minister draws particular attention to the fact that EU foreign ministers, during their last meeting, have called on the Albanian authorities to respect the basic principles of democracy," the statement said.
"I regret that these appeals have so far not been heeded and I am warning of the dangers of more mass unrest, which would be a loss for everybody," the minister said.

Albania's beleaguered government issued orders to shoot armed rioters on sight, imposed a dusk-to-dawn curfew and curbed press freedoms on Monday in an effort to smother violent unrest sweeping Europe's poorest country.

The unrest was sparked by the collapse of pyramid investment schemes that climaxed at the weekend when at least 12 people were killed after crowds in several southern towns raided weapons depots and went on a rampage of violence.
